title: Console audit trail view for Dedicated rollout actions (promote/abort/override/hold)
creator: Kenji Nakamura
project: Dedicated staged rollouts for reserved pools
description:
Goal
Design an audit trail view in Redwood Console for Dedicated staged rollout actions (create/update/promote/abort/hold/force actions) with filters, export UX, and RBAC-aware (admin-only) fields.

Context
Dedicated staged rollouts introduce explicit stage promotions with gates and override escape hatches (force-promote, hold, force-rollback). Regulated and enterprise customers (and our internal SRE/oncall) need an auditable record of:
- who did what, when, and why
- what changed (stage, plan, policy)
- whether it was an override
- what evidence/gates were evaluated at the time
- how this ties back to change management processes and incident review

Non-goals (v1)
- Full SIEM configuration workflow in Console (we’ll support export/download and rely on existing audit export pipelines where available)
- Arbitrary custom audit event types outside staged rollouts

Primary personas
1) Customer Admin (Dedicated): needs change record, basic filtering, download for internal change tickets.
2) Redwood Operator / SRE: needs full fidelity, internal-only fields, and fast navigation during incidents.
3) Security / Compliance reviewer (customer + Redwood): needs retention/export story, tamper-resistant semantics (immutable log), consistent event schema.

Information architecture
Entry points
A) Dedicated Pool → Rollouts tab → “Audit” sub-tab (default scoped to this pool)
B) Rollout Plan detail view → “Change history” (stage-by-stage timeline + deep link to audit event)
C) Global Console (admin/internal): Org → Audit Logs (filtered by category=Rollouts/Dedicated)

Event list (table)
Columns (customer-visible)
- Timestamp (with timezone toggle; default account locale)
- Actor (user email / service principal name; if unavailable, show “System”)
- Action (Promote stage / Abort rollout / Hold rollout / Resume / Force promote / Force rollback / Update plan / Create plan)
- Target (Pool name + region if relevant; linkable)
- Rollout plan (name/version; linkable)
- Stage (from → to, e.g., “10% → 50%” or “partition 1/10 → 5/10”, matching ADR stage model)
- Outcome (Succeeded / Rejected / No-op / Failed)
- Reason (free text; truncated with hover/click)

Columns (admin-only / internal)
- Actor type (human / service account / system automation)
- Actor org + role (RBAC role at time of action, if available)
- Request ID / Idempotency key
- Source (Console / API / Automation)
- Client IP (if captured and approved for display)
- Authorization context (policy decision summary: “force_promote allowed by role=dedicated_admin”)

Row details (drawer)
Clicking a row opens a right-side drawer with:
- Event header: action, timestamp, actor, outcome
- “What changed” diff block:
  - state transition (e.g., running → held)
  - stage pointer changes (previous_stage_id, new_stage_id)
  - traffic split/partition params (read-only summary, not raw routing config)
- Gate summary at action time (when applicable):
  - Gate evaluation status (Pass / Fail / Unknown)
  - Evaluation window (e.g., last 15m)
  - Gate list: error rate, p95, saturation/headroom, OOM rate, GPU health
  - For each: observed value, threshold, sample size (if available), and link to stage dashboard
  - If override was used: “Override: Force promote” with required justification text + warning banner
- Links:
  - “View rollout plan”
  - “View stage dashboard” (Observability dashboards)
  - “Copy event ID”
  - “Download single event (JSON)” (admin-only initially)

Filters + search
Default scope depends on entry point (pool / plan / org).
Filter controls (top bar, collapsible on smaller widths):
- Date range (preset: 1h, 24h, 7d, 30d + custom)
- Action type (multi-select)
- Outcome (multi-select)
- Actor (typeahead; customer org users; admin can search across)
- Pool (typeahead; admin-only for global view)
- Region (multi-select; only shown when pool is multi-region)
- Rollout plan (typeahead)
- “Overrides only” toggle
- Free text search (reason, event ID, actor)

Export UX
Customer-visible
- “Download CSV” and “Download JSON” for current filtered result set
- Inline warning copy: “Exports may contain sensitive operational metadata. Handle per your organization’s policies.”
- Hard limit (v1): export up to N rows (proposed 10k) with guidance to narrow date range

Admin/internal
- “Export to audit pipeline” is out of scope for v1 UI; however provide:
  - “Copy filter as query” (stringified query params) for internal tooling
  - “Download JSON (includes admin fields)”

RBAC + visibility rules (design requirements)
- Customer Admin should see:
  - actions initiated by their org users
  - system actions that impacted their pool (auto-abort, auto-rollback, policy blocks) but without leaking Redwood internal operator identity unless explicitly allowed by policy; show actor as “Redwood Operator” or “System” depending on the event type (needs Security signoff)
- Redwood internal roles should see full actor identities and admin-only fields.
- Force actions require explicit “Reason for override” input and show prominently in list and details.

States and empty/error handling
- Empty state: “No rollout audit events in this time range.” with suggested presets.
- Permission error: “You don’t have access to view audit logs for this pool.” include link to docs/contact admin.
- Partial data: if gate evidence is missing (telemetry lag), show “Gate evidence unavailable at time of export” and avoid rendering as failure.

Visual + interaction notes
- Keep audit list visually consistent with other Console audit surfaces (if any), but optimized for rapid scanning during incidents.
- Use a dedicated “Override” badge in the Action column for force-promote/force-rollback.
- “Outcome: Rejected” should include a short cause label (e.g., “RBAC” / “State conflict” / “Missing metrics fail-closed”) in the drawer.

Open questions / decisions needed
1) Redwood operator identity exposure: For customer admins, do we show named Redwood employees for manual actions? Current recommendation: default to “Redwood Operator” and include a stable operator ID only in export (or only for internal). Needs Security + Product signoff.
2) Retention messaging: What retention window do we commit to showing in Console vs exporting? (Align with audit logging spec.)
3) Gate evidence snapshot: Do we persist a snapshot at action time vs always recompute? UI should assume snapshot is available; if backend only provides references, we need to reflect that clearly.
4) Multi-region: If promotion is partial by region, does each region generate a separate event or one event with region breakdown? UI supports both, but prefers single event with region sub-lines in drawer.
5) Customer export expectations: Some regulated accounts will require JSON event payloads that match the audit event schema exactly. Decide whether to export “raw audit event” vs “UI formatted.”

Deliverables
- Figma: audit list + drawer, filter bar, export modal, empty/error states
- UX copy for override flows and export warnings
- Spec notes for engineering: column mapping, RBAC hiding rules, export formatting expectations

Acceptance criteria (for design)
- Supports both pool-scoped and global audit views
- Clearly surfaces override actions and their justification
- Provides export flows for filtered results
- Defines admin-only fields and how they are hidden/redacted for customer users
- Includes handling for missing gate evidence / telemetry lag

Links
- Confluence audit event spec: sources/confluence/security-and-compliance/audit-logging/audit-events-for-dedicated-rollout-actions.json
- Related design: DES-431-stage-timeline-component-for-dedicated-rollouts (timeline links into audit)
- Console backend endpoints (in progress): ENG-5980-console-backend-endpoints-for-stage-promotion

Design notes (implementation-friendly)
- Prefer server-driven columns/fields (backend returns a “redactions” hint) to avoid client needing to know compliance logic.
- Ensure event IDs are stable and can be referenced in support tickets.
- Export should reflect the same RBAC redactions as the UI by default.
comments: 2025-02-13 — Marissa Cole: Please prioritize the pool-scoped version first; global org audit view can come in v1.1. Also, we need deep links from the rollout plan page into audit events for change mgmt screenshots.

2025-02-14 — Kaitlyn Nguyen: +1 on redacting Redwood employee identities by default for customer users. We should treat operator identity as sensitive unless contractually required. If needed, provide an “Operator ID” that maps internally only.

2025-02-18 — Chloe Martin: Backend can provide event list + details via a single endpoint; export could be handled client-side for small sets, but we prefer a server-side export job for >10k rows. Can design include a “We’ll email you when ready” pattern as optional?

2025-02-20 — Kevin Osei: For compliance reviews we’ll need JSON export that mirrors the audit event schema closely. Ideally the export option includes both “Raw JSON” and “CSV (human-readable)” for customers.

2025-03-03 — Rafael Mendes: During incidents, we need to see whether a promotion was blocked due to missing metrics (fail-closed) vs actual threshold breach. Please make sure the drawer calls out the failure reason distinctly.
2025-03-07 — Lauren Bishop: Please include an “Overrides only” toggle and make sure force-promote shows a warning banner; customers asked for this explicitly during beta check-ins.
